summary: Limbang Airport (LMN/WBGJ) is a regional airport serving the town of Limbang in northern Sarawak, Malaysia, on the island of Borneo. The town is geographically distinctive as it is an exclave separated from the rest of Sarawak by Brunei territory, making air travel a convenient link to other parts of the state. The airport primarily handles turboprop flights connecting passengers to Miri and other Malaysian Borneo destinations.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate from Limbang Airport?
A: MASwings (a subsidiary of Malaysia Airlines) operates regular turboprop services connecting Limbang to Miri and other destinations in Malaysian Borneo.

Q: How far is Limbang Airport from the town center?
A: The airport is located a short drive from Limbang town center, typically around 5-10 minutes by car.

Q: Are there international flights from Limbang Airport?
A: No, Limbang Airport primarily serves domestic routes within Malaysian Borneo, mainly to and from Miri.

Q: Is the airport used for general aviation?
A: While primarily a commercial facility, the airport can accommodate general aviation traffic and occasional charter operations serving the region.
transport_tips: Taxis and ride-hailing services are available at the airport for the short trip into Limbang town. Car rental can be arranged in advance for travelers wanting to explore the surrounding Limbang Division independently. Pre-booking transport is recommended as the airport has limited ground transport options compared to major hubs.
local_tip: If you're connecting through Miri, allow extra time for luggage and transfers, as same-day connections to destinations like Kuching or Kota Kinabalu are common and worth booking on a single ticket to avoid rebooking hassles.
